searchText: up until now it feels there's support for this latest change. It's merged alread and I'd say we then also go with it if there's no opposition with good arguments against. cc <@429719902363058177> <@680337202521440470> <@281967554572976128> <@628018527470616606> <@902806914252021830> Yeah we agree with this change. Nimbus EL's EVM already worked this way so that the delegated address wouldn't appear in the BAL when prior checks fail. It makes sense to do the minimal state lookups and the BAL should only include the state read/touched. please keep in mind that the PR from <@774033563732541451> needs to be extended to cover top level calls as well (process_message_call). Which currently behaves differently than inner calls. There might be a gap in tests wrt top level calls as well. It is discrepancy, we are adding eip7702 delegation to the access list, while the account is not loaded in BAL. This is especially hard in revm as access list is not separate structure in Journal but the State map that is used to store account is used as access list, that same structure is used to create BAL. It is most performant way to handle journal access. Could we move access list inclusion to be after those check for caller balance and call depth? It would require some workaround for us but it is possible to do. It is a simple and reasonable rule to record state access only when access is necessary and Besu already works this way, so I think Besu is OK with the change. so the delegation cost is deducted from inner frame's gas? Just adding it to access list is delayed after those checks That is fine too, but moving the cost as well makes more sense to me. But it might be a worse breaking change. It is strange, that now child call needs to arbitrary pay for gas. For revm, charging gas and then loading it again would be basically mean an additional hashmap, but that should be okay.

excerpts.author: b.hartnett
excerpts.content: Yeah we agree with this change. Nimbus EL's EVM already worked this way so that the delegated address wouldn't appear in the BAL when prior checks fail. It makes sense to do the minimal state lookups and the BAL should only include the state read/touched.
